data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 offers a genuine test: real reliability gain occurs only when semantic drift lets the panel catch errors the checklist author was blind to. But this test is self-defeating as a discriminating criterion within a single evaluation. The problem asks for evidence that separates genuine gain from mere compliance that tracks the right answer. Under SRC_002's own framing, when the panel's divergent interpretation happens to match the verifiable outcome, that is indistinguishable from the case where the checklist's encoded intent already contained the correct answer and the panel merely complied. SRC_002 needs an additional observable—e.g., cases where the panel corrects a checklist item the author demonstrably got wrong—to separate drift-driven correction from coincidence. Without specifying how to tell, within one evaluation, whether panel success stems from beneficial drift versus the checklist already being right, the proposed discriminator fails the problem's requirement.
